activities.title: High School SynBio Intro Lecture
activities.description: We delivered an introductory session on synthetic biology for Grade 10 and 11 students. The session covered gene circuits and protein design, introducing how biology, engineering, and computation come together in synthetic biology.

activities.title: High School Protein Design Lecture
activities.description: We introduced rational and AI-assisted protein design using published case studies and examples from our own project. The lecture explored how researchers use protein structures to guide mutations and develop new designs through an iterative process of testing and refinement.

activities.title: High School SynBio Market and Career Analysis Lecture
activities.description: This online session introduced students to the synthetic biology industry and its career opportunities. We explored different career paths and how scientific research can be turned into commercial products, helping students better understand the field before choosing their future studies.

activities.title: Primary School SynBio Intro Workshop
activities.description: We introduced the basic concepts of synthetic biology to Grade 5 students at Keyuan Primary School in Shenzhen through everyday applications and hands-on activities. Students created clay models of organisms they imagined and extracted DNA from strawberries.

activities.title: Geraniol Lab Session
activities.description: This workshop targeted high school students at our own school, Shenzhen College of International Education (SCIE). We aimed to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical experience by guiding students through a series of connected laboratory procedures.

activities.title: Middle School SynBio Intro Workshops
activities.info: Nanshan Foreign Language Middle School & Nanning No. 3 Middle School
activities.description: Students explored basic synthetic biology concepts and carried out strawberry DNA extraction activity. One workshop included an ethical debate on using gene editing to create superheroes, while the other featured an English reading activity on the benefits and risks of synthetic biology.

activities.title: Online Discussion Group
activities.description: We kept an online discussion group open after our lectures, allowing students to ask follow-up questions and share ideas. Discussions covered protein modelling, synthetic biology applications, industry challenges, and university choices.

activities.title: iGEM Club
activities.description: Our school club introduced students to synthetic biology and the iGEM competition. Sessions covered topics ranging from the central dogma to DNA assembly, alongside laboratory activities, murder mystery games, and debates that offered members different ways to explore the subject.

activities.title: SynBio Ethics Debate
activities.description: Our SynBio ethics debate invited students from different academic backgrounds to explore the question: “If synthetic biology could eliminate human suffering, should we prioritise enhancing human capabilities or preserving human life in its natural state?” Through preparation, debate and interviews, participants explored the possibilities of SynBio while reflecting on the ethical boundaries.

activities.title: SynBio Collaboration Fair
activities.description: In collaboration with the SMS and Yucai SZ iGEM teams, we organised a SynBio fair at Honey Park, inviting local families and park visitors to explore synthetic biology through hands-on activities. Visitors built microbial cell models using clay, discovered everyday applications of SynBio through posters, and learned signs for scientific terms in an interactive Sign Language Challenge.

activities.title: SynBio-Vocab Seminar
activities.description: We organised a SynBio Vocabulary Learning Seminar for local families at Xiang'an Community in Shenzhen. Participants shared their challenges and strategies in learning scientific English, while our Biology Vocabulary Booklet introduced a different approach to understanding biological terminology. The booklet included explanations of word roots and suffixes, biological examples and short quizzes

activities.title: Bacteria-Fungi Clay Kit
activities.description: We created a clay kit for building bacterial and fungal cell models. The kit also included microbial identity cards and instruction booklets introducing microbial cell structures, their functions and the everyday applications of these microorganisms.

activities.title: Bacteria-Fungi Fuse Beads
activities.description: We published free, downloadable fuse bead patterns featuring different microorganisms, allowing people to explore SynBio through a creative activity at home. Each design was accompanied by brief notes highlighting key cellular structures, their roles and how these microorganisms are used in everyday life.

activities.title: Lab-Themed Jubensha Mystery Game
activities.description: Students took part in a lab-themed Jubensha (murder mystery game) centred on a failed PCR experiment. By analysing gel images, reagent records and PCR settings, they worked together to identify the cause of the failure, applying their laboratory knowledge through evidence-based reasoning and collaborative problem-solving.

activities.title: Song of SynBio
activities.description: We wrote a song to the melody of “Do-Re-Mi” to help students review molecular biology and genetic engineering. Its three verses covered concepts such as codons and base pairing, and techniques including PCR, gel electrophoresis, and transformation.

activities.title: Dance of Central Dogma
activities.description: Students performed a dance illustrating transcription and translation, with each taking on the role of a biological component, such as a nucleotide, ribosome or amino acid. Their movements showed how these components work together, bringing the flow of genetic information to life and making it easier to visualise.

activities.title: Long Videos
activities.description: We published long-form videos on Bilibili and YouTube, exploring different ways to introduce SynBio. Our video on Craig Venter and the Human Genome Project explored the history of genome sequencing, while our other videos included a recording of an AI-assisted protein design club session and a laboratory ASMR video capturing everyday lab sounds.

activities.title: Short Videos
activities.description: We published 13 short videos on RedNote and WeChat Channels. Our official RedNote account, GreatBay-SCIE 2026, has gained over 92,000 likes and saves, along with more than 5,200 followers. Our short videos combined humour with familiar laboratory scenarios to introduce basic experimental procedures and safety practices. Topics included microbial cultivation, the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), and the importance of keeping food and drinks out of the laboratory.

activities.title: Infographics
activities.description: We published a series of illustrated posts exploring synthetic biology through our iGEM project and related scientific research. Covering topics such as the biological basis of body odour, fragrance production using engineered microorganisms and AI-assisted protein design, these posts helped readers understand the scientific principles behind SynBio and how they can be applied to real-world problems.
